title: app: create_job/resume_signal abort the whole shell — Supervisor::drive uses raw tokio::spawn from the GTK main thread (kills e2e, CI #65–#70)
body:
## Symptom

CI runs #65–#70, `app-e2e` job, step "Drive the shell once": the app boots (boot dump shows `url=tauri://localhost title=IUM`), the test fills the form, the submit button enables — the **click on Upload kills the WebDriver session**:

```
panicked at ium-e2e/tests/e2e_shell.rs:505:29:
click Upload: "wd 500 Internal Server Error unknown error: Session terminated without a reply
(POST /element/node-2E90502E-7FE0-4B91-92AA-9A12569AC7D3/click {})"
```

The driver log tail (app stderr is piped through WebKitWebDriver → tauri-driver) ends with a Rust backtrace and:

```
thread caused non-unwinding panic. aborting.
```

Runs #65–#69 never even reached the click (submit never enabled — the one-shot live-progress contradiction, fixed by leg A driving the tus adapter in 9cb2e81). **Run #70 is the first CI run in history that clicked Upload — and the shell died on it.**

## Root cause

Tauri v2 docs (Calling Rust from the Frontend, Async Commands section):

> "Commands without the *async* keyword are executed on the main thread."

`create_job` and `resume_signal` are **synchronous** `#[tauri::command]`s, so their bodies run on the GTK main thread. Both call `Supervisor::drive()`, and `ium-core/src/supervisor.rs` drives jobs with a **raw `tokio::spawn`**. `tokio::spawn` requires an entered tokio runtime context on the calling thread — the GTK main thread has none (tauri's global async runtime is not *entered* there; this is exactly why `tauri::async_runtime::spawn` exists).

So the first Upload click panics with "must be called from the context of a Tokio 1.x runtime"; the unwind crosses the webview IPC handler (a C/GTK FFI boundary), which Rust aborts outright → the whole shell process dies → WebKitWebDriver reports the session terminated → e2e red.

Unit tests never caught it because every test constructs and drives the `Supervisor` inside `#[tokio::test]` where the context exists. The e2e is doing exactly what #35 built it for: catching what unit tests structurally cannot.

## Fix direction

* `Supervisor` captures a `tokio::runtime::Handle` at construction (context present) or accepts one explicitly (`Supervisor::with_handle`); `drive()` spawns through the stored handle — callable from ANY thread, no ambient context required.
* `ium-app` setup constructs the supervisor with `tauri::async_runtime::handle()`.
* RED test in `ium-core`: drive a supervisor from a thread with NO runtime context — today it panics, after the fix it must drive (job reaches a journal-true terminal state).

## Also

* `scripts/app-e2e.sh` kept only `tail -25` of driver.log, which cut off the actual panic message and cost a full diagnosis cycle — forensics must print the full tail.
* CI run #62's red is a concurrency-cancelled `core (macos-latest)` job (pseudo-failure); `cancel-in-progress` produces red noise the board then has to explain — it goes.
